events.title: A great earthquake strikes Aleppo and northern Syria
events.description: An earthquake struck Aleppo and northern Syria a day after a smaller shock, causing damage and chaos across the area. The toll of 230,000 later reported by Ibn Taghribirdi probably conflated it with other earthquakes.
events.html: An earthquake struck Aleppo and northern Syria a day after a smaller shock, causing damage and chaos across the area. The toll of 230,000 later reported by Ibn Taghribirdi probably conflated it with other earthquakes.

events.title: The Treaty of Shaoxing between Jin and Song is ratified
events.description: The Treaty of Shaoxing, signed in 1141, was formally ratified when a Jin envoy visited the Song court. The Southern Song gave up its claims north of the Huai, including Kaifeng, and agreed to a yearly tribute to the Jin.
events.html: The Treaty of Shaoxing, signed in 1141, was formally ratified when a Jin envoy visited the Song court. The Southern Song gave up its claims north of the Huai, including Kaifeng, and agreed to a yearly tribute to the Jin.

events.title: Pope Leo X names Henry VIII 'Defender of the Faith'
events.description: Pope Leo X granted Henry VIII the title Fidei Defensor for his treatise attacking Martin Luther. Henry later broke with Rome, yet British monarchs still use the title, abbreviated 'F.D.' on coins.
events.html: Pope Leo X granted Henry VIII the title Fidei Defensor for his treatise attacking Martin Luther. Henry later broke with Rome, yet British monarchs still use the title, abbreviated 'F.D.' on coins.

events.title: Catholic cantons defeat Zürich at the Battle of Kappel
events.description: Near Kappel am Albis, the Catholic cantons of central Switzerland defeated Protestant Zürich, and the reformer Huldrych Zwingli, who accompanied the Zürich army as chaplain, was killed. The Second Peace of Kappel halted the spread of the Reformation in the Confederacy.

events.title: A British force defeats Benedict Arnold's fleet at Valcour Island
events.description: On Lake Champlain, a British force under General Guy Carleton captured or destroyed most of the American fleet commanded by Benedict Arnold. The American defence of the lake nonetheless stalled British plans to reach the upper Hudson River valley.
events.html: On Lake Champlain, a British force under General Guy Carleton captured or destroyed most of the American fleet commanded by Benedict Arnold. The American defence of the lake nonetheless stalled British plans to reach the upper Hudson River valley.

events.title: The Second Boer War begins in South Africa
events.description: War broke out when Britain let a Boer ultimatum expire. In the three-year conflict that followed, British concentration camps saw the deaths of about 26,000 Boer women and children and many thousands of black Africans.
events.html: War broke out when Britain let a Boer ultimatum expire. In the three-year conflict that followed, British concentration camps saw the deaths of about 26,000 Boer women and children and many thousands of black Africans.

events.title: Roosevelt receives Einstein's warning about atomic bombs
events.description: The economist Alexander Sachs delivered to Franklin Roosevelt a letter signed by Albert Einstein, warning that Germany might build a uranium bomb. Roosevelt set up an advisory committee that led eventually to the Manhattan Project.
events.html: The economist Alexander Sachs delivered to Franklin Roosevelt a letter signed by Albert Einstein, warning that Germany might build a uranium bomb. Roosevelt set up an advisory committee that led eventually to the Manhattan Project.

events.title: Pope John XXIII opens the Second Vatican Council
events.description: More than 2,000 bishops gathered in St Peter's Basilica for the opening of the Second Vatican Council. Over three years it introduced vernacular liturgy, embraced ecumenism and affirmed religious freedom.
